newsitem.title: UK: UK's Partners Holdings plans float, expansion.
newsitem.headline: UK's Partners Holdings plans float, expansion.

text.p: Specialist stationary retailer Partners Holdings Plc said on Thursday it was planning a float on the London Stock Exchange on April 28 to fund an expansion in its store chain.
The company said it had raised 5.05 million stg after expenses through a placing at 150p per share, valuing the company at 28 million stg.
Partners operates 80 specialist retail stores but said its planned strategy was to increase its number of stores to 220 by the year 2001.
Peter Davey, chief executive, said Partners will attain the pre-tax forecast of two million stg for the year to March 31 1997 against 1.15 million for the previous year.
Davey compared Partners' position in the market to toiletries retailer Superdrug, part of retailing conglomerate Kingfisher Plc.
"Superdrug concentrates on tolietries which is only part of what the likes of Boots do and they sit happily side-by-side in the high street," said Davey.
"Similarly, we concentrate on stationary and we are to WH Smith and John Menzies, what Superdrug is to Boots."
Ten percent of Partners' 2,500 core lines are "own-label" products and Davey said the company aims to keep ahead on product design.
"Stationary can be black and white but we like to make it colourful and interesting," he said.
